sections.label: The result
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: 154 Entered. 101 Failed. 53 Cleared Every Check.

visual.purpose: Aligned fill and session strips introduce the three views and the one-veto rule.

sections.label: The result
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: This is one recorded test using the Dow data. The number we carry forward is 53. It is a count of candidates at one step in the process.

visual.purpose: Aligned fill and session strips introduce the three views and the one-veto rule.

sections.label: The result
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The key question is how 101 candidates failed across three checks. We cannot add the three failure counts as if every failure were different. A failure set is a list of candidate IDs, so the same ID can appear more than once.

visual.purpose: Aligned fill and session strips introduce the three views and the one-veto rule.

sections.label: The setup
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The test began with 154 candidates from the Dow branch. Before any check runs, that starting list is the whole population for this lesson.

visual.purpose: A fixed candidate rail makes the 154-entry cohort visible before any failure set is counted.

sections.label: The setup
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The list stayed the same while the execution fill and clock changed. Each candidate faced one frozen rule under those new conditions. The comparison stays fair: the candidate changes only when the test changes the condition.

visual.purpose: A fixed candidate rail makes the 154-entry cohort visible before any failure set is counted.

sections.label: The setup
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: This is a screen. A pass opens the next question. That leaves fewer candidates to inspect.

visual.purpose: A fixed candidate rail makes the 154-entry cohort visible before any failure set is counted.

sections.label: The setup
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The three checks use a later fill and two session halves. They ask the same basic question from three angles: does the result hold when the trade arrives differently?

visual.purpose: A fixed candidate rail makes the 154-entry cohort visible before any failure set is counted.

sections.label: Fill and slippage
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A fill is the price the trade gets when the order enters or exits. Imagine a signal at the end of a bar: the fill is the price attached to the actual entry or exit.

visual.purpose: A signal-to-fill arrow makes the one-bar-later fill stress concrete.

sections.label: Fill and slippage
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A backtest often uses the signal price as if that were the fill. That is convenient for calculation, but it can make a trade look cleaner than the path a real order takes.

visual.purpose: A signal-to-fill arrow makes the one-bar-later fill stress concrete.

sections.label: Fill and slippage
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Slippage is the gap between the price you expect and the price you get. A small gap changes the dollars won or lost on every trade, so a long run can feel that gap many times.

visual.purpose: A signal-to-fill arrow makes the one-bar-later fill stress concrete.

sections.label: Fill and slippage
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Here the test moves the entry one bar in the same direction. That gives the fill price a simple stress. Every candidate gets the same treatment, which makes the comparison repeatable.

visual.purpose: A signal-to-fill arrow makes the one-bar-later fill stress concrete.

sections.label: Fill and slippage
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The test answers one question about the fill. The test does not model every broker or every order. The controlled comparison is valuable on its own. It says nothing about a particular execution desk.

visual.purpose: A signal-to-fill arrow makes the one-bar-later fill stress concrete.

sections.label: Latency is a different question
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Latency is the time from the signal to the fill. If the market moves while an order is waiting, that time can change the price of the trade.

visual.purpose: Two axes separate time latency from price slippage without conflating them.

sections.label: Latency is a different question
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Slippage is price. Latency is time. Both can change an entry. Keeping the words separate helps us ask the right question about the test.

visual.purpose: Two axes separate time latency from price slippage without conflating them.

sections.label: Latency is a different question
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: This one-bar move stands in for a later fill. The shift gives a repeatable stress for the recorded test. The same shift is applied across the candidate list, so the result is comparable.

visual.purpose: Two axes separate time latency from price slippage without conflating them.

sections.label: Latency is a different question
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A rule that needs the perfect entry has a timing weakness. This check makes that weakness visible. The weakness can be small in one trade and large across a population.

visual.purpose: Two axes separate time latency from price slippage without conflating them.

sections.label: The session split
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A split sample is a method that puts the same trades into separate groups before you measure them. The rule stays fixed; only the group used for the measurement changes.

visual.purpose: A median-hour divider creates two session halves from the same trade stream.

sections.label: The session split
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The middle entry hour divides this intraday run into session half 1 and session half 2. That boundary gives both groups a declared place in the day.

visual.purpose: A median-hour divider creates two session halves from the same trade stream.

sections.label: The session split
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A session half is one of those groups. It tells us whether the result leans on one part of the day. A strong combined result can hide a weak morning or afternoon group.

visual.purpose: A median-hour divider creates two session halves from the same trade stream.

sections.label: The session split
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The rule keeps a candidate when profit factor clears 1.0 after the fill move and in both session halves. One candidate must clear the fill check plus both clock checks.

visual.purpose: A median-hour divider creates two session halves from the same trade stream.

sections.label: Why hours can matter
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A regime is a stretch of market behavior. One rule can meet a different market in a different stretch. One stretch can trend, while another moves sideways or changes speed.

visual.purpose: Clock segments are shown as conditions that can carry or weaken a result.

sections.label: Why hours can matter
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Price and volume can change across the trading day. Session splitting gives us a way to check that change. It asks whether the result travels with the clock instead of with the rule.

visual.purpose: Clock segments are shown as conditions that can carry or weaken a result.

sections.label: Why hours can matter
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A result can look strong in one stretch and weak in another. This test stays inside its recorded window. This keeps the lesson tied to the evidence we actually have.

visual.purpose: Clock segments are shown as conditions that can carry or weaken a result.

sections.label: Why hours can matter
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The split can expose a candidate whose result depends on one clock segment. It cannot explain why the segment matters, but it can show where to ask next.

visual.purpose: Clock segments are shown as conditions that can carry or weaken a result.

sections.label: Three views, one rule
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The one-bar fill check rejects 41 candidates. Session half 1 rejects 66, and session half 2 rejects 23. These are separate counts from the same recorded run.

visual.purpose: Three aligned strips show 41, 66, and 23 failure sets against the same 154 candidates.

sections.label: Three views, one rule
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: All three counts start with the same 154 candidates. Each count answers a different version of the same stress question.

visual.purpose: Three aligned strips show 41, 66, and 23 failure sets against the same 154 candidates.

sections.label: Three views, one rule
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Session half 1 produces the largest count. A single total would hide the clock segment creating the most removals. The separate strips preserve that information.

visual.purpose: Three aligned strips show 41, 66, and 23 failure sets against the same 154 candidates.

sections.label: Three views, one rule
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The rule is simple: one failed check drops a candidate. The candidate needs three passes. One impressive number cannot carry it.

visual.purpose: Three aligned strips show 41, 66, and 23 failure sets against the same 154 candidates.

sections.label: Why the counts overlap
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Some candidates fail twice, so adding the three counts would count them twice. Counting a candidate twice would make the population look weaker than it is.

visual.purpose: Overlapping sets and inclusion-exclusion arithmetic show why the union is 101.

sections.label: Why the counts overlap
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The fill set shares 24 candidates with session half 1 and 5 with session half 2. Those shared IDs are the reason the headline number needs a union.

visual.purpose: Overlapping sets and inclusion-exclusion arithmetic show why the union is 101.

sections.label: Why the counts overlap
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The two session halves share zero candidates. All three sets share zero. The pairwise overlaps are the only overlaps in this recorded output.

visual.purpose: Overlapping sets and inclusion-exclusion arithmetic show why the union is 101.

sections.label: Why the counts overlap
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Start with 41 plus 66 plus 23. Take away 24 and 5. The total is 101. This is the inclusion and exclusion step in plain arithmetic.

visual.purpose: Overlapping sets and inclusion-exclusion arithmetic show why the union is 101.

sections.label: Why the counts overlap
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: A union counts a candidate once when it appears in any set. It answers the practical question: how many unique candidates failed one or more checks?

visual.purpose: Overlapping sets and inclusion-exclusion arithmetic show why the union is 101.

sections.label: The weak row
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Candidate formula-2309285457-3105 has profit factor 1.123246 after shifting the fill by one bar. That first number clears the cutoff.

visual.purpose: The exact 3105 row visibly turns red on session half 1 while the other views stay green.

sections.label: The weak row
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Its session half 1 value is 0.986603. That is below the 1.000000 cutoff. The difference looks small, but the rule still treats the value as a fail.

visual.purpose: The exact 3105 row visibly turns red on session half 1 while the other views stay green.

sections.label: The weak row
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Its session half 2 value is 1.494639. Two strong views cannot erase the weak middle view.

visual.purpose: The exact 3105 row visibly turns red on session half 1 while the other views stay green.

sections.label: The weak row
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: One value below the cutoff disqualifies the candidate. Every check must clear the cutoff. This is the crisis in the run: the row looks good until the session is separated.

visual.purpose: The exact 3105 row visibly turns red on session half 1 while the other views stay green.

sections.label: Profit factor as one diagnostic
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Profit factor compares the dollars won with the dollars lost in the same set of trades. The numerator is gross winning dollars; the denominator is gross losing dollars.

visual.purpose: Gross winning and losing dollars define PF as one diagnostic with a threshold.

sections.label: Profit factor as one diagnostic
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Above 1 means more dollars won than lost in that set. At 1.0, the two sides are equal before the rest of the research questions are asked.

visual.purpose: Gross winning and losing dollars define PF as one diagnostic with a threshold.

sections.label: Profit factor as one diagnostic
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: It leaves out account size. It also leaves out drawdown and fill cost. A ratio can summarize one ledger while hiding the path that produced it.

visual.purpose: Gross winning and losing dollars define PF as one diagnostic with a threshold.

sections.label: Profit factor as one diagnostic
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Profit factor is one diagnostic inside this test. The other checks still matter. A pass here means the ratio cleared its cutoff in this view.

visual.purpose: Gross winning and losing dollars define PF as one diagnostic with a threshold.

sections.label: The row that survives
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Candidate formula-2309285457-3088 records 1.080180 with the fill shifted one bar. The first value is above the same cutoff.

visual.purpose: The exact 3088 row keeps all three values above 1.000000.

sections.label: The row that survives
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Its session half 1 value is 1.156412, and session half 2 is 1.151833. Both clock groups stay above 1.0 in this row.

visual.purpose: The exact 3088 row keeps all three values above 1.000000.

sections.label: The row that survives
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: All three values clear 1.000000, so the candidate passes this test. Each of the three values carries the pass.

visual.purpose: The exact 3088 row keeps all three values above 1.000000.

sections.label: The row that survives
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: That is a recorded pass for this run. It is one result inside the research process. The next step still has its own question and its own evidence.

visual.purpose: The exact 3088 row keeps all three values above 1.000000.

sections.label: From 154 to 53
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: When we remove the 101 candidates counted in the union, 53 remain. The union gives us the clean population count.

visual.purpose: The union subtraction resolves into 154 minus 101 equals 53.

sections.label: From 154 to 53
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: 154 candidates entered. 101 failed on one or more checks. 53 passed all three. The three numbers describe one pipeline step from start to finish.

visual.purpose: The union subtraction resolves into 154 minus 101 equals 53.

sections.label: From 154 to 53
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The subtraction works because each union member appears once. It prevents overlapping failures from being subtracted twice.

visual.purpose: The union subtraction resolves into 154 minus 101 equals 53.

sections.label: From 154 to 53
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: These are survivors of one test. Later questions still matter. This shorter list is easier to study, but it is not the end of the study.

visual.purpose: The union subtraction resolves into 154 minus 101 equals 53.

sections.label: What the pipeline proves
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The numbers come from the recorded Dow run. They are not an invented example. The candidate IDs and values come from that same run, along with the counts.

visual.purpose: Real-data and wiring proof are separated from the false validated flag.

sections.label: What the pipeline proves
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The run used real market data. The pipeline connections also ran. That tells us the route executed; it leaves other research questions open.

visual.purpose: Real-data and wiring proof are separated from the false validated flag.

sections.label: What the pipeline proves
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The run record marks validated as false. The word validated stays reserved for evidence that clears more than this one screen.

visual.purpose: Real-data and wiring proof are separated from the false validated flag.

sections.label: What the pipeline proves
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: I want the math to be repeatable. Another person can rebuild those sets and get the same count. That is the standard for a useful research step.

visual.purpose: Real-data and wiring proof are separated from the false validated flag.

sections.label: A beginner's worksheet
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Start with the 154 IDs that enter the test. Keep the starting list separate from the lists that fail.

visual.purpose: A beginner can reproduce the three sets, union, and veto rule as a small worksheet.

sections.label: A beginner's worksheet
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Make a set for the fill view and separate sets for the two session halves. Give every set a clear name before you count it.

visual.purpose: A beginner can reproduce the three sets, union, and veto rule as a small worksheet.

sections.label: A beginner's worksheet
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Write the three profit factors for every candidate. Remove a row when a value is at or below 1.0. This is the all-three rule written as a small table.

visual.purpose: A beginner can reproduce the three sets, union, and veto rule as a small worksheet.

sections.label: A beginner's worksheet
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Take the union once. Compare its size with the entering count. Then check that the remainder is the passing list.

visual.purpose: A beginner can reproduce the three sets, union, and veto rule as a small worksheet.

sections.label: A beginner's worksheet
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Keep one failed row and one passing row. A row shows how the rule works. The two examples make the population count concrete.

visual.purpose: A beginner can reproduce the three sets, union, and veto rule as a small worksheet.

sections.label: The boundary
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: The test ends with 53 survivors. That is the boundary of this episode.

visual.purpose: The lesson ends at 53 and names cost stress as the next question without importing later results.

sections.label: The boundary
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: Cost stress is the follow-up. Raise the fill and commission assumptions and count what remains. That question belongs to the 53 that pass this test, while 154 is the starting group.

visual.purpose: The lesson ends at 53 and names cost stress as the next question without importing later results.

sections.label: The boundary
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: That belongs to the next test. This episode stops before its result. We carry the question forward and wait for that answer.

visual.purpose: The lesson ends at 53 and names cost stress as the next question without importing later results.

sections.label: The boundary
sections.speaker_directions: Plain beginner teaching; state the mechanism, then its boundary.
sections.text: For now, the lesson is simple: the rule must survive the price it may receive and the hours that carry the result. A clean total is the beginning of that discipline.

visual.purpose: The lesson ends at 53 and names cost stress as the next question without importing later results.
